Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 28013 of 2024

Applicant :- Awadhesh Sonker @ Dancer
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Piyush Shukla,Pratyush Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Piyush Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.1 of 2024, under Sections 420 IPC, Police Station Ghatampur, District Kanpur Nagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text: Police Station Ghatampur, District Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown person and according to the FIR, two unknown persons by playing fraud received Rs.
58,000/- from the informant while he was in bank and during investigation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter on the basis of his confessional statement.

4. He further submitted that as per prosecution from the possession of the applicant Rs. 2100/-
were also recovered.

sentences.text:
He further submitted that entire allegation levelled against the applicant is false and actually applicant is having criminal history of 19 other cases and only due to previous criminal history of the applicant, he has been made accused by the police in the present case.
6.
He further submitted that entire criminal history of the applicant has been explained in the instant bail application.
7. He further submitted that there is no cogent evidence against the applicant on record which can show that applicant duped the informant in any manner.

8. He further submitted that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate Ist class punishable with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 26.4.2024.
9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, as per allegation, applicant alongwith one another by playing fraud received Rs.
58,000/- from the informant while he was in the bank and he is also having criminal history of 19 other cases but it reflects that there is no cogent evidence against the applicant on record except the confessional statement of the applicant.

12. Further, after considering the criminal antecedents of the applicant, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that only due to previous criminal antecedents, applicant has been made accused in the present matter, cannot be ruled out, at this stage.
13. Further, criminal history of the applicant has been explained in the instant bail application.
14. Further, law is settled that ordinarily, if otherwise case of bail is made out then on the basis of criminal history of the accused, his bail application should not be rejected.
15. Further, all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate Ist class punishable with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 26.4.2024.

16. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant-Awadhesh Sonker @ Dancer, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court Awadhesh Sonker @ Dancer vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159789737/
2 concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
19.

20. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
